updateDocument looks up the document only via documentRepository.findById(request.getId()); the entityType/entityId from the URL path are never used to scope the lookup. Any caller with document-write permission on any entity can update (and overwrite the file of) any document by ID regardless of its actual parent entity. The sibling read method DocumentReadPlatformServiceImpl.retrieveDocument correctly uses findByIdAndParentEntityTypeAndParentEntityId, showing the scoped lookup exists but is not used here.

extra.message: url is read verbatim from the Hook's stored 'Payload URL' configuration field (set from the Hook create/update REST request body with no scheme/host/IP allowlist) and passed to processorHelper.createWebHookService(url), which builds a Retrofit client with baseUrl(url) and issues an HTTP request to it. Any user able to create/update a webhook can make the Fineract server send requests to arbitrary internal hosts (e.g. cloud metadata endpoints) on every matching business event.

"Validation" of the user-supplied payload URL (fieldValue, from the create/update-hook request body) is implemented by making a live outbound HTTP request to it via processorHelper.createWebHookService(fieldValue).sendEmptyRequest().execute(), with no host/IP allowlist. This triggers an SSRF at hook save time to any attacker-chosen destination.

A connection is opened to a user/report-template-supplied url and TrustModifier.relaxHostChecking(connection) is applied unconditionally, installing an always-true HostnameVerifier and a TrustManager that accepts any certificate, while the current user's Basic-Auth credentials are attached via the Authorization header. This allows MITM interception of credentials sent to any URL referenced from a report/template, with no opt-in/dev-only guard.

fineract.database.defaultMasterPassword defaults to the literal "fineract" unless FINERACT_DEFAULT_MASTER_PASSWORD is overridden. This value is used by DatabasePasswordEncryptor as the AES key to encrypt/decrypt tenant datasource passwords stored in the tenants table; anyone with read access to the tenants DB plus knowledge of this published default can decrypt every tenant's real DB credentials.

server.ssl.key-store-password defaults to the literal "openmf" unless FINERACT_SERVER_SSL_KEY_STORE_PASSWORD is overridden, protecting the keystore.jks shipped inside the jar at the classpath default. Anyone with the distributed artifact and knowledge of this well-known default can extract the TLS private key used for server TLS termination.

fineract.security.cors.allowed-origin-patterns defaults to "*" while fineract.security.cors.allow-credentials defaults to true. Wired into Spring's CorsConfiguration (setAllowedOriginPatterns("*") + setAllowCredentials(true)), this reflects any requesting Origin back in Access-Control-Allow-Origin while sending Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, permitting credentialed cross-origin requests from any site by default.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: sanitize() only calls Path.of(path).normalize(), which collapses '../' segments syntactically but does not reject a result that still contains unresolved leading '..' or re-validate it stays under the configured root. The path is built in DocumentWritePlatformServiceImpl.createDocument/updateDocument from request.getFileName() (the raw multipart Content-Disposition filename, only null/length-checked by FileUploadValidator) joined into '<prefix>/<entityType>/<entityId>/<fileName>', then resolved against the root folder in FileContentStoreService. A filename like '../../../../etc/cron.d/x' lets an authenticated user with upload rights write files outside the configured content root.

reportParams entry values (sourced from user-supplied 'R_'-prefixed query parameters, validated only when the parameter's registered format type is number/date) are concatenated into normalizedFileName with no character filtering, which is later placed into a Content-Disposition response header by the CSV export service. A CRLF or quote/semicolon in an unregistered or string-typed R_ query value flows into the response header.
